detail: Known: the SUN DAY Campaign reading of EIA Electric Power Monthly (https://solarquarter.com/2026/02/25/sun-day-campaign-and-eia-data-show-renewables-supplied-nearly-26-of-u-s-electricity-in-2025-led-by-solar-wind-and-battery-storage/) gives utility-scale solar 6.54 percent of total generation in 2025 when small-scale is counted in the total; ours, against utility-scale generation only, 6.8 percent. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known in part: the Global Carbon Project (via Drishti IAS, https://www.drishtiias.com/daily-updates/daily-news-analysis/india-s-carbon-emission-growth-slows-in-2025) gives India about 3.19 billion tonnes of fossil CO2 in 2024; ours, EIA international data for energy, 2,871.8 million tonnes, about 10 percent lower (cement and other sources outside energy are part of the difference). Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known in part: the Global Carbon Budget 2024 (https://globalcarbonbudget.org/fossil-fuel-co2-emissions-increase-again-in-2024/) gives China 32 percent of 37.4 billion tonnes of fossil CO2 in 2024, about 12.0 billion; ours, EIA international data for energy, 12,715.9 million tonnes, about 6 percent higher. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known: World Nuclear News (https://world-nuclear-news.org/articles/entergy-retires-vermont-yankee-after-42-years) records Vermont Yankee closing on 29 December 2014, and EIA Today in Energy (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=19811) that it gave about 72 percent of Vermont generation; a share of 0.0 since follows. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known in part: the International Gas Union (via Gulf Times, https://www.gulf-times.com/article/705813/business/qatar-accounts-for-188-share-of-global-lng-exports-in-2024-igu) gives Qatar 77.2 million tonnes of LNG in 2024 (about 10.4 Bcf a day); ours, EIA dry gas exports by all routes including pipeline, 4,438.8 Bcf (12.2 a day). Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known: the figure is EIA State Energy Data System own expenditure estimate (https://www.eia.gov/state/seds/seds-data-complete.php?sid=CA); its California table was not seen in the search result. Ours: 66.02 billion USD in 2024 against 18.42 in 1990. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known: OPEC (via Construction World and Hellenic Shipping News, https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/?p=1068769) puts India 2024 oil demand at 5.59 million barrels a day; EIA Today in Energy (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=64084) names India the largest source of oil demand growth in 2024; ours 5,599 thousand. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known in part: Columbia Center on Global Energy Policy (https://www.energypolicy.columbia.edu/irans-natural-gas-paradox-vast-resources-limited-export-capacity/) gives Iran 263 billion cubic metres in 2024 and OPEC about 278 (9,300 to 9,800 Bcf); ours, EIA dry production, 9,852.8 Bcf, at or above the top of that range. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known in part: Our World in Data (https://ourworldindata.org/co2/country/indonesia) gives Indonesia 812 million tonnes of territorial CO2 in 2024; ours, EIA international data for energy, 886.8 million tonnes, about 9 percent higher: the two sources differ. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known in part: China coal output (4.76 billion tonnes) and imports (542.7 million tonnes) were records in 2024 (Mysteel, https://www.mysteel.net/news/5074522-nbs-chinas-2024-coal-output-hits-record-high); no national consumption total found; ours, EIA international data, 5,453.4 million short tons. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known in part: China National Bureau of Statistics (via Mysteel, https://www.mysteel.net/news/5074522-nbs-chinas-2024-coal-output-hits-record-high) gives a record 4.76 billion tonnes in 2024, about 5,250 million short tons; ours, EIA international data, 4,852.9 million short tons, about 7.5 percent lower: the two sources differ. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known in part: High Country News (https://www.hcn.org/articles/solar-and-wind-continue-to-push-coal-off-the-wests-grid/) gives solar 14 percent of the generation of 11 western states in 2025; ours covers the eight states of EIA Northwest region: 8.0 percent in 2025. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known in part: the Global Carbon Project series (via Statista, https://www.statista.com/statistics/1282696) gives India 2,032 million tonnes of CO2 from coal in 2023 and projected coal emissions up 4.5 percent in 2024; ours, EIA international data, 2,117.1 million tonnes in 2024. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known in part: China National Energy Administration (via Rigzone, https://www.rigzone.com/news/wire/gas_coal_production_in_china_at_record_high_last_year-17-jan-2025-179341-article/) gives a record 246.4 billion cubic metres in 2024, about 8,700 Bcf; ours, EIA international data, 9,127 Bcf, about 5 percent higher: the two sources differ. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known: EIA Today in Energy (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=67205) gives 15 GW of battery storage added in 2025; ours, the units that entered service in 2025 and still operate in EIA-860M, 16,372 MW. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known: EIA Today in Energy (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=64844), from Cedigaz, gives Australia LNG exports between 10.2 and 10.7 Bcf a day over 2020 to 2024; ours 3,740 Bcf in 2024 (10.2 a day). Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known in part: Berkeley Lab Queued Up 2024 edition (https://emp.lbl.gov/sites/default/files/2024-04/Queued%20Up%202024%20Edition_R1.pdf) gives about 1,030 GW of storage active in the queues at the end of 2023, a stock; ours is the flow of new battery requests in a year from Berkeley Lab data, 157,429 MW in 2024. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known in part: FPL says 11 percent of its 2025 energy was solar (Florida Phoenix, https://floridaphoenix.com/2026/09/30/byron-donalds-says-solar-power-is-a-fad-but-florida-utilities-are-expanding-its-use/), and LowCarbonPower (https://lowcarbonpower.org/region/Florida) about 9.5 percent utility-scale for September 2025 to August 2026; ours, statewide utility-scale from EIA, 9.3 percent in 2025. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known: EIA Electric Power Monthly table 5.1 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/monthly/epm_table_grapher.php?t=epmt_5_1, opened 19 November 2026) prints 1,503,310 thousand MWh of commercial sales for 2025 and 1,450,941 for 2024; the draft repeats EIA own total and sets it against 2001 (1,083.1 TWh).

Known in part: EIA Today in Energy (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=53819) gives the carbon intensity of US generation at 854 pounds per MWh (387 kg) in 2020, down 18 percent from 2016; ours, from EIA power-sector CO2 and generation, 362 kg per MWh in 2022 against 604 in 2001. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known in part: Utility Dive (https://www.utilitydive.com/news/duke-energy-apologizes-for-winter-storm-outages-as-ferc-nerc-open-investig/639583/) reports Duke rolling blackouts in the Carolinas during Elliott, the first there, and a FERC and NERC inquiry; no publisher found printing the Carolinas region highest hour against the same days of other years. Ours: 44,630 MW, 24.3 percent above the mean of 2018 to 2025. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known: PJM preliminary figures (https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/committees-groups/committees/oc/2025/20250710/20250710-item-10---june-2025-hot-weather-update.pdf) give 161,770 MW on 23 June and 162,401 MW on 24 June 2025, its third and fourth highest peaks; ours, EIA-930 Mid-Atlantic, 160,560 MW, 1.1 percent lower. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known: ERCOT Monthly Operational Overview, January 2026 (https://www.ercot.com/files/docs/2026/02/18/ERCOT-Monthly-Operational-Overview-January-2026.pdf) gives a preliminary January peak of 75,572 MW on 26 January 2026, below the winter record of about 80,500 MW of February 2025; ours 75,599 MW. Ours adds the comparison with the same days of 2019 to 2025. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known in part: EIA Today in Energy (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=66144) gives Canada about 14 percent of New England supply in 2016 to 2022 and 5 percent in 2024 and in the first eight months of 2025; ours, the mean hourly flow from Canada to New England, 432 MW in 2025 against 1,945 MW in 2019. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known in part: EIA Today in Energy (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=66144, September 2025) says daily net imports from Canada into New England averaged under 40 percent of 2022 in January to August 2025, with days of net exports to Canada; no publisher found counting the hours power flowed from New England to Canada. Ours: 29.5 percent of 2025 hours against 0.0 in 2019. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known in part: CAISO 2025 statistics (https://www.caiso.com/documents/2025-statistics.pdf) give peak net exports of 7,380 MW on 12 June 2025, and Grid Status (https://blog.gridstatus.io/batteries-boom-but-solar-slides-in-caiso/) describes CAISO as a midday net exporter from 2023 to 2025; no publisher found counting the share of hours California exported on net. Ours: 5.0 percent of 2025 hours against 0.4 percent in 2019. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known in part: NukeWorker (https://www.nukeworker.com/outages/unit/palo-verde-1/), from NRC daily reports, lists Palo Verde refueling outages of 43 days (unit 1, spring 2025) and 60 days (unit 3, autumn 2025); no publisher found printing the plant share of capacity on outage by year. Ours: 9.9 percent in 2025 against 20.7 in 2007. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known: Fraunhofer ISE (https://www.ise.fraunhofer.de/en/press-media/press-releases/2024/status-quo-one-year-since-germanys-nuclear-exit-renewable-capacity-expands-electricity-from-fossil-fuels-significantly-reduced.html) records the last German reactors closing on 15 April 2023; a share of 0.0 in 2025 follows. The draft repeats a known event. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known: Statistics Indonesia, via The Coal Hub (https://thecoalhub.com/indonesian-coal-exports-up-by-over-8-percent.html) and Reuters reports, gives a record 557.8 million tonnes exported in 2024 (about 615 million short tons) and calls Indonesia the largest thermal coal exporter; ours, EIA international data, 614.8 million short tons. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known: EIA state profile for Florida (https://www.eia.gov/state/?sid=FL) gives natural gas about 75 percent of 2024 generation, and EIA Today in Energy (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=60221) 31 percent in 2002 and 75 percent in 2022; ours 73.0 percent in 2025 against 22.8 in 2001. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known in part: EIA state profile for New Mexico (https://www.eia.gov/state/analysis.php?sid=NM) gives coal about 21 percent of its 2024 generation, down from 63 percent a decade before; a Greater Phoenix briefing (https://www.gpec.org/wp-content/uploads/Arizonas-Energy-Grid-Feb-2025.pdf) gives Arizona 10 percent in 2023. No publisher found printing the two states together. Ours: 11.2 percent in 2025 against 55.4 in 2001. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known: EIA Today in Energy (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=64544) estimates China consumed 16.3 million barrels a day of petroleum and other liquids in 2024; ours, EIA international data, 16,371 thousand. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known in part: EIA Electric Power Annual table 2.8 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/annual/html/epa_02_08.html) prints commercial sales by state, and notes that changes from 2023 to 2024 in the commercial and industrial sectors largely reflect better reporting of data centers and crypto mining. Ours, from SEDS: 55.2 TWh in 2024 against 23.7 in 1990. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known: the figure is from EIA Monthly Energy Review; GreenTechLead (https://greentechlead.com/renewable-energy/u-s-eia-renewable-energy-hits-8-385-quadrillion-btu-in-first-11-months-of-2025-52419) gives about 8.6 percent for January to November 2025 and EIA Today in Energy (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=67684) a record renewable production; ours 8.6 percent for 2025. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known: Ember (https://ember-energy.org/latest-insights/european-electricity-review-2026/2025-at-a-glance/) gives wind 27 percent of Finnish electricity in 2025, a record; Renewables Finland (https://suomenuusiutuvat.fi/en/wind-power-statistics-2025/) 27.9 percent. Ours, Eurostat net production: 27.9 percent. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known: Brazil regulator ANP (via MercoPress, https://en.mercopress.com/2026/02/05/brazilian-oil-and-gas-production-record-in-2025-4-987million-boe-d) gives crude of 3.77 million barrels a day in 2025, a record, 12.3 percent above 2024; ours, EIA international data, 3,769 thousand. Seen in search results, page not opened.

New as far as found: PJM (https://services.pjm.com/annualreport2025/operations/) reports a solar record of nearly 12,000 MW on 18 April 2025 and its net-load paper describes the evening net peak; no publisher found printing solar output in PJM tightest hours as a share of capacity. Ours: 34.4 percent in 2025 against 19.3 percent in 2019. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known: EIA state profile (https://www.eia.gov/state/analysis.php?sid=NV) gives all solar 31 percent of Nevada generation in 2024; LowCarbonPower (https://lowcarbonpower.org/region/Nevada) about 30 percent utility-scale over July 2025 to June 2026. Ours, utility-scale from EIA: 30.8 percent in 2025. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known in part: Modo Energy (https://modoenergy.com/research/ercot-battery-buildout-2025-annual-report) gives 13.9 GW of operating batteries in ERCOT entering 2026, and ERCOT peak demand reached 91.1 GW in 2026; no publisher found printing the fleet against the mean of the ten highest days. Ours: 19.9 percent in 2025 against 0.2 percent in 2019. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known in part: an analysis of Census data (NCCER fact sheet, https://www.nccer.org/media/2026/05/Private-Construction-Spending-Patterns-Fact-Sheet-2026.pdf) gives data centers 3.3 percent of all nonresidential construction in 2025 (41 billion USD, an earlier vintage); ours, against private nonresidential only and the current vintage, 6.35 percent. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known: Portuguese reports of 2025 (Energia Estrategica, https://energiaestrategica.com/renewables-set-new-record-in-portugal-covering-nearly-70-of-power-demand-in-2025/) say imports covered 17 percent of Portugal demand in 2025, down from 20 in 2024; ours, from Eurostat, 17.7 percent of electricity available. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known: Ember European Electricity Review 2026 (https://ember-energy.org/EER2026) says Greece cut coal to about 5 percent of its electricity in 2025; ours, from Eurostat net production, 5.3 percent. The draft repeats Ember headline. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known in part: Ember (https://ember-energy.org/latest-insights/solar-met-61-of-us-electricity-demand-growth-in-2025/) gives New Mexico solar rising from 7 to 17 percent over the 24 months to October 2025 (all solar); Climate Central gives wind and solar about 20 percent in Arizona. No publisher found printing utility-scale solar for Arizona and New Mexico together. Ours: 14.0 percent in 2025 against 0.0 in 2001. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

New as far as found: studies of wind and solar droughts found are European (Wood Mackenzie, https://www.woodmac.com/ja/press-releases/wood-mackenzie-study-reveals-critical-risks-of-europes-dunkelflaute-renewable-energy-droughts/); no publisher found counting CAISO hours with wind and solar far below usual. Ours: 2,776 hours in 2025 against 2,180 in 2019, on the ERW definition. Seen in search results, page not opened.

New as far as found: EIA Weekly Natural Gas Storage Report (https://ir.eia.gov/ngs/ngs.html) prints each week against the five-year average and range; no publisher found counting the weeks a year that South Central salt lay outside its five-year range. Ours: 13.5 percent of weeks in 2025 against 67.3 percent in 2015. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known: EIA Natural Gas Annual table 9 (https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/Annual/pdf/table_009.pdf) gives 2024 LNG exports of 4,367 Bcf and pipeline exports of 3,339 Bcf (7,706 together); EIA Today in Energy (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=64844) calls the US the largest LNG exporter in 2024. Ours, EIA international data, 7,707 Bcf. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known in part: Climate Change Tracker (https://climatechangetracker.org/nations/greenhouse-gas-emissions/china/sources-of-co2-emissions) gives China gas CO2 of about 890 million tonnes in 2024, a record; ours, EIA international data, 831.9 million t in 2024 against 30.8 in 1980 (a different source and method). Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known in part: Modo Energy (https://modoenergy.com/research/ercot-battery-buildout-2025-annual-report) gives the average duration of ERCOT batteries, 1.65 hours at the start of 2026; no publisher found printing battery energy per MW of solar. Ours: 0.72 MWh per MW of solar in 2025 against 0.04 in 2015. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known: Texas 2036 (https://texas2036.org/news-analysis/texas-oil-production-evolution-of-a-giant-2000-2025/), from EIA data, gives Texas 42.34 percent of US oil production in 2025; ours 42.2 percent. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known in part: the Alliance for Automotive Innovation (https://www.autosinnovate.org/posts/press-release/2025-q4-get-connected-press-release, March 2026) gives all electric vehicles at 2.5 percent of light-duty vehicles in operation in 2025, and EIA (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=68325) 2 percent in 2024; ours counts battery electric only, from the Alternative Fuels Data Center: 1.94 percent in 2025. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known in part: Berkeley Lab Queued Up, 2025 edition (https://emp.lbl.gov/sites/default/files/2025-12/Queued%20Up%202025%20Edition%20-%2012.15.2025.pdf), gives 77 percent of the capacity requested from 2000 to 2019 withdrawn by the end of 2024 (all types) and a 14 percent completion rate for solar in the 2024 edition; the draft reads Berkeley Lab data by year of exit (76.0 percent of solar MW leaving in 2024 withdrawn). Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known in part: BLS (via FRED, https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/IPUJN518W010000000) counts about 497,400 employees in NAICS 518 in 2023, a different measure; the Census Bureau publishes County Business Patterns 2023 (https://www.census.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2025/2023-county-business-patterns.html) from which ours, 629,527, is summed over the states. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known: the figure is the Alternative Fuels Data Center's own count; NACS Magazine (https://www.nacsmagazine.com/Issues/March-2026/The-State-of-Charging-in-the-United-States, March 2026), citing it, gives 67,948 public DC fast ports; ours 68,599 for 2025. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known in part: EIA's Short-Term Energy Outlook (via Power Engineering, https://www.power-eng.com/coal/coal-stockpiles-at-plants-to-remain-healthy/) expected power-sector coal stocks of about 116 million short tons at the end of 2025; EIA's Today in Energy (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=65787) gives 124 million on 1 June 2025. Ours, the December figure from EIA's monthly fuel stocks: 109.7 million short tons in 2025 against 161.6 in 2008. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known in part: EIA's Today in Energy (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=64424, January 2025) says Pennsylvania's power sector burned 1.0 Bcf a day of gas in 2013 and 2.6 in 2023; the Natural Gas Annual table S40 (https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/Annual/pdf/table_S40.pdf) gives 996 Bcf delivered to power in 2024. Ours, from EIA's State Energy Data System: 1,032 trillion Btu in 2024 against 14 in 1990. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known in part: Nebraska Public Media (https://nebraskapublicmedia.org/en/news/news-articles/nebraskans-cope-with-rising-demand-prices-for-electricity/), citing OPPD, says data centers used 1 percent of OPPD's sales in 2018 and 21 percent in 2024; no publisher found printing OPPD's commercial sales by year. Ours: 7.88 TWh in 2025 against 3.67 TWh in 2017. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Ours: 9.94 degree days a day in 2024 against 8.93 in 2019. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Ours, from EIA's state-to-state capacity table: 25.38 Bcf a day in 2025 against 7.87 in 1990. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known: EIA's nuclear explainer (https://www.eia.gov/energyexplained/nuclear/us-nuclear-industry.php) gives a 2025 capacity factor of 91 percent, and NukeWorker (https://www.nukeworker.com/outages/industry_stats.php), from the NRC's daily power reports, 91.38 percent; ours, the mean daily power level from the same NRC reports, 91.1 percent. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known: the figure is EIA's own international series (republished by The Global Economy, https://www.theglobaleconomy.com/India/coal_production/, 1,371 million short tons for 2024); the IEA's Global Energy Review 2025 (https://www.iea.org/reports/global-energy-review-2025/coal) calls India's 2024 coal demand an all-time high. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known in part: EIA's Today in Energy (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=67844, July 2026) gives US crude output of 13.6 million barrels a day in 2025, about 40 percent above Russia and Saudi Arabia; no publisher found printing the US share of world petroleum and other liquids. Known: EIA's Uranium Marketing Annual Report 2025 (https://www.eia.gov/uranium/marketing/) gives a US-origin share of enrichment of 23 percent in 2025; ours 22.8 percent. The draft repeats EIA's own figure. Seen in search results, page not opened.
